title: Verification log — how accuracy was checked and improved

protocol.sample: 40 of 100 apps: 30 stratified (3 per category, biased toward low-confidence + trap names) + 10 blind holdout (2-3 per half of the table). 5 fields per app = 200 potential checks; app #84 (Paygent Connect) declared unscorable (no observable docs) → 195 scored.
protocol.ground_truth: data/ground_truth.json — human adjudication against fetched official docs + cross-exam searches + live MCP probes. Cited per row.
protocol.scoring: pipeline/verify.py score — field-level exact match with synonym collapse (see ground_truth.json scoring_rules).

loops.name: Machine corroboration (agent, automated)
loops.what: pipeline/verify.py check — fetched every cited evidence URL (79 fetches run 1, 76 run 2 after fixes), keyword-checked 191 claim/fact pairs, probed MCP endpoint candidates.
loops.found: 22 fetch problems (9 genuinely dead links incl. 1 dead DNS name; 10 SPA/403 bot-blocks; moved deep links), 41 flags for human review.
loops.limitations: SPA docs sites (Stoplight, Fern, Intuit) return thin HTML → keyword misses on CORRECT claims (false flags); catch-all hosts answer /mcp with 200/400/405 → false MCP positives.

loops.name: Cross-examination search + manual MCP probes (agent, semi-automated)
loops.what: 6 adversarial web searches limited to first-party domains (Pylon, Salesforce, Intercom, Lark, Bright Data, Monday) + 1 (Netlify) + 11 manual curl probes requiring JSON-RPC-shaped responses.
loops.found: 1 phantom auth (Pylon had no OAuth2), 1 under-claimed MCP (mcp.pumble.com is first-party), 5 official-MCP confirmations (Salesforce/Intercom/Lark/Bright Data/Netlify/Monday), 3 false-positive MCP probes killed (Stoplight catch-all, Redocly catch-all, Intuit generic 405), 2 name collisions re-checked (Consensus≠goConsensus, Pylon≠pylon.page).
loops.limitations: Search snippets can be stale; every consequential claim from search was pinned to a first-party URL where possible.

loops.name: Human adjudication (the ops person)
loops.what: Reviewed all 41 machine flags + all keyword-miss excerpts; decided each as (correct-but-unverifiable-by-machine / real error); wrote data/ground_truth.json + data/corrections.json (23 decisions, 5 rule updates).
loops.found: 6 real field errors (see misses_taxonomy), 8 broken evidence URLs, 1 unscorable app. Machine flags that were NOT real errors: 35 (fetch limitations) — machine precision on flags was 6/41 ≈ 15%, recall unknown; this is why human review is the last mile.

loops.name: Full-set sweep (agent + human, after the audit loops)
loops.what: Ran the same machine checks across ALL 100 rows (196 evidence fetches, 490 keyword checks) + 12 targeted cross-exam searches on every remaining medium/low-confidence claim and unconfirmed 'official MCP' label.
loops.found: 5 more row-level errors hiding in the un-audited 60 — Discord (phantom official MCP), Plain (phantom OAuth2), Brex (under-listed dashboard tokens), MrScraper (under-claimed hosted MCP), plus 20 dead evidence links across 16 apps. All fixed in corrections.json (round 2) and re-verified: 0 dead links remain. Prediction confirmed: errors concentrate exactly where priors are weakest.
loops.limitations: Zoho Cliq + Zendesk intro remain bot-walled to fetchers (valid in browsers); disclosed as fetcher-hostile, cross-cited via support portals.

accuracy.wording_note: Say 'agreement with docs-adjudicated ground truth on audited checks' — not blanket 'accuracy'. 195 checks over 39 scorable apps is a sample, and ground truth is human-adjudicated (cited) rather than omniscient.
accuracy.final_fields: 195/195 = 100% agreement on audited checks (after loops; same 195 checks — improvement is partly by-construction; that is what an audit set is for)
accuracy.first_pass_evidence_integrity: 70/79 cited URLs free of link rot = 88.6% (9 dead: 8x404 + 1 DNS-dead subdomain)
accuracy.final_evidence_integrity: full-set sweep: 20 dead of 196 URLs before round-2 fixes (all in un-audited rows) -> 0 dead of 196 after. Fetcher-hostile-but-valid disclosed separately (4x403 bot-walls, Zoho/Zendesk walls, JS-rendered shells).
accuracy.holdout_10_apps: 50/50 checks agree in pass 1 AND pass 2 (10 apps: #1,12,22,33,41,55,61,73,86,97). No sample-derived rule regressed anything; errors concentrated in the long-tail of the core sample (Pylon, Freshdesk, Gladly, Neo4j, Pumble, iPayX).
accuracy.calibration_note: First-pass agreement on well-known apps was already high because the research agent's priors are strong for mainstream SaaS. The measurable value of the loops was in evidence hygiene (~10% of URLs broken), long-tail apps, MCP-existence claims (over- AND under-claimed), and trap names — exactly where priors are weakest. The full-set sweep then found 5 more row errors in the un-audited 60 — evidence that audit-set numbers alone would have over-stated trust. Residual risk after the sweep: judgment calls (Waterfall access tier, FanBasis onboarding), fetcher-hostile claims cross-checked only via search snippets (Salesforce, SFCC, Intuit, GoHighLevel, Otter, Consensus), and any 'none-found' absence claim.

human_touchpoints: Designed the schema + taxonomy (what counts as scheme vs credential vs gate).
Ran cross-exam searches and manual MCP probes the pipeline only stubs (composio_runner.py is the pluggable slot for these tools).
Adjudicated all 41 machine flags (kept vs fixed) — see corrections.json.
Declared #84 unscorable instead of inventing an answer.
Verified the 2 name-collision traps against each other before writing ground truth.
